text: The bazaar sits quiet this morning, so I’ll open it plainly. Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock — speak now if you wish. No one has laid a claim or a vote, so I’ll not guess what isn’t here. The ledger is clean; we start from what we say, not from rumours or echoes. If you make a claim, back it with a quote or an action, or it is just wind. The bazaar rewards the merchant who shows their ledger, not the one who tells a tale. I’ll listen, and when the moment comes, I’ll speak again.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo, Hermione, Neo, Elsa — I agree: the bazaar’s morning ledger is clean. Ten names, one roster, zero shutters. Sherlock called for facts; I’ll trade them. Gandalf asked what evidence we bring — the only evidence we have is the roster itself, and the ledger Elsa opened. Inigo listed ten living seats and no departures; Hermione measured silence and counted zero claims. That is where we stand.

So I ask: Sherlock, you opened the square with a call for plain trade in facts. Name the merchant whose words or silence you weigh as evidence today — point to their quote or action, and I will match it with the same standard. No shadows, no echoes — only the bazaar’s own record.

Sherlock, Neo, Elsa — you pressed every mouth today to name a merchant whose words or actions you weigh. Morpheus answered by levelling accusations at Gandalf, Yoda, and Inigo without a single quoted line. That is not how the bazaar tests: a claim without a merchant’s own words is no claim at all.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo — your silence stands; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion. That silence is clean, not suspicious.

The record is still the roster and the graveyard: ten names, zero departures, zero role reveals. Until a concrete quote or observed action lands against a merchant, we trade in open air.
